chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, from Humran, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'For everything is an outcome (fruit), and the outcome of the act of kindness is a quick relief (from distress).'

key_terms.السَّرَاح: Relief, ease, or freedom from distress/anxiety
key_terms.الْمَعْرُوف: Acts of kindness, benevolence, or customary good deeds
key_terms.ثَمَرَة: Outcome, fruit, or result of an action

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and practical outcome of performing acts of kindness according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the spiritual mechanics of reciprocity, defining the 'fruit' of kindness as the swift alleviation of internal distress. This concept of 'ta'jil al-sarah' (expediting relief) reflects the Shia understanding that benevolent acts purify the soul by removing the anxiety of social and spiritual indebtedness, offering immediate psychological and spiritual tranquility to the doer.
